analyst_view.overall: Ajax (11th of 36, 6 points) host FC Thun (19th, 3 points). Ajax have won six of their last seven and beat ADO Den Haag 3-0 on Sunday, but lost 18-year-old midfielder Jorthy Mokio late in that game: he has a broken fibula, has had surgery and is out until about late February, and the numbers' missing list for Ajax is empty, so they don't know. Julian Brandt, Sofyan Amrabat and Anton Gaaei are back, Bissouma is not registered for Europe, and Dolberg, Adingra and Tsygankov are long-term absences already in Ajax's form. Míchel called Thun 'the most important match' and said he is not thinking about Sunday's Klassieker at Feyenoord, so heavy rotation now looks less likely than I assumed yesterday. Thun lost 3-2 at Young Boys, miss defenders Montolio and Saiz long-term, have striker Furkan Dursun and midfielder Mattias Käit doubtful with back problems, and face three games in a week after this; no referee is named yet.

goals.text: The numbers say 4.2 goals, 3.2 of them for Ajax, and already add 4% for Ajax's 16 goals in their last six and Thun's leaky defence. What they can't see is Mokio's broken fibula (he scored in the 3-0 against ADO and was in the expected eleven) and Thun's main striker Dursun being doubtful; Brandt's return softens the first, so I trim 4%, to about 4.0 goals. I dropped the rotation argument because Míchel says Thun is the priority.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.3 corners, 6.5 of them Ajax's, against a Thun side that usually has well under half the ball. Losing Mokio changes who plays in midfield more than how much Ajax attack down the flanks, and recent corner form on both sides is already counted. I stay at 9.3.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.2 cards, with Thun expected to collect more (2.6) chasing the ball, and both sides' recent bookings are already in. No referee is named in the brief and nothing points to a heated night between two clubs with no history. I stay at 4.2.

shots.text: The numbers say 30.4 shots, about 20 of them Ajax's, and already add 3% for Ajax's recent volume (21 shots against ADO). Without Mokio and with Thun possibly missing Dursun up front, I take off 2%, to about 29.8 shots; Ajax at full strength otherwise should still dominate the ball.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.6 shots on target and already take about 6% off Thun for their weak recent accuracy. Thun's best finisher Dursun is a doubt and Ajax lose one of their scoring midfielders in Mokio, neither known to the numbers, so I trim 3%, to about 9.3. Thun's long-term injured defenders are already in their form.
